# Shorting via perps vs borrow and sell mechanics — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Shorting via perps vs borrow and sell mechanics. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] A perpetual-futures short is a derivative position, not a loan of the asset. A long and a short counterparty agree a price without exchanging anything except margin posted with the venue; no underlying has to be acquired, so there is nothing to borrow or deliver; and the contract never expires. Because nothing forces convergence at maturity, a funding payment from one side to the other (peer-to-peer; Hyperliquid collects no fee on it) is the mechanism that pulls the perp price toward spot. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2212.06888v7 · keywords: Shorting via perps vs borrow and sell mechanics · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/funding

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] On crypto venues a spot short is the same borrow-and-sell trade, funded from a lending pool whose price moves with conditions. Kraken says funds from its BTC margin pool let a client short sell, charges the fee on the quantity of the asset sold (its BTC example: 'could be 0.010%'), locks the rollover rate at order execution and states that margin rates fluctuate with market conditions. Aave's variable borrow rate is a two-slope function of pool utilization, with a second slope applying from the optimal usage ratio to 100 percent utilization, set per reserve. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-28) — https://support.kraken.com/articles/206161568 · keywords: Shorting via perps vs borrow and sell mechanics · also: https://aave.com/docs/aave-v3/smart-contracts/interest-rate-strategy

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A correct perp short can still be force-closed by auto-deleveraging (ADL). When an account goes bankrupt and liquidators and the insurance fund cannot absorb it, venues close profitable opposite-side positions against it. Orderly: ADL fires only if liquidators do not take over, nobody claims the positions from the insurance fund, and the insurance fund margin ratio is below its minimum; it selects the traders with the most profit and the most leverage. Hyperliquid: opposite-side users are ranked by unrealized PnL and leverage and closed at the previous mark price against the underwater account. WuBlockchain's example is a crash where longs go bankrupt and the profitable shorts are cut. Campbell et al. define ADL as a rule-based way to spread losses across solvent participants. (high confidence) — https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/insurance-fund-and-adl · keywords: Shorting via perps vs borrow and sell mechanics · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/auto-deleveraging, https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15963, https://wublock.substack.com/p/hyperliquid-activates-cross-margin
- [statement] ADL candidate ranking is venue-specific, so check the venue's docs before assuming who gets cut. Orderly ranks by profit and leverage; Hyperliquid sorts by (mark_price / entry_price) * (notional_position / account_value); Campbell et al. show that for single-asset isolated margin, reducing the highest-leverage accounts first (a 'minimax leverage' water-filling rule) is optimal for all monotone risk measures. (medium confidence) — https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/insurance-fund-and-adl · keywords: Shorting via perps vs borrow and sell mechanics · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/auto-deleveraging, https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15963

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A perp short carries basis risk that a borrow-and-sell short does not, because it is short the contract rather than the asset. He et al.: perpetuals 'are not guaranteed to converge to the spot price', and deviations from no-arbitrage prices in crypto are larger than in traditional currency markets (though they diminish over time). BIS researchers find 'excess volatility' of crypto futures relative to spot prices (a futures-wide finding, not perp-specific). (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2212.06888v7 · keywords: Shorting via perps vs borrow and sell mechanics · also: https://www.bis.org/publ/work1087.htm
